item.name: 06 - Devices and sessions (ORB-004)
item.description:
Depends on ORB-003 (sign-in). Registers and verifies its own user, then signs in as several simulated devices (via distinct User-Agent headers) to exercise GET /sessions, DELETE /sessions/{id}, and POST /sessions/sign-out-others.

Assumptions flagged here rather than silently baked in -- confirm each before trusting the corresponding test:
1. Field names on the list response (deviceLabel, lastUsedAt, location, currentDevice, id) are inferred, since SessionSummaryResponse itself wasn't available to check against.
2. AC3 asks for both 'location and address' as separate things; only a single 'location' field is asserted here pending confirmation of the real DTO shape.
3. Request '06 Cannot sign out the device you're using' encodes a guard that is NOT stated in any of the 12 acceptance criteria and wasn't confirmed against SessionService. Delete it if that guard doesn't actually exist.
4. Access-token revocation is tested as immediate (request 09), not just refresh-token revocation, because the API contract states the sid claim's purpose is explicitly 'so a specific session can be revoked.' If JwtAuthenticationFilter turns out not to check session status per request, this expectation and that filter need to be reconciled together.
5. 'Unknown device' (not 'Unrecognised device') is the exact string DeviceLabelResolver returns -- verified against that file directly.
6. Request 22 (AC11, password change revokes other sessions) is a placeholder: no change-password endpoint has been documented in any contract seen so far. Fill in the real method/URL before relying on it.

item.name: 07 Sign out Device B from Device A
08 List reflects the sign-out, Device A still present and still current (AC: entry gone, others remain, current device still signed in)

exec: pm.test('returns 200 - Device A is still signed in', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('Device B entry is gone', () => pm.expect(body.some(s => s.id === pm.collectionVariables.get('sessionIdOtherB'))).to.be.false);
pm.test('Device A entry remains, marked current', () => pm.expect(body.some(s => s.id === pm.collectionVariables.get('sessionIdCurrentA') && s.currentDevice === true)).to.be.true);

item.name: 09 Device B's access token is rejected immediately after sign-out (AC: signed-out device is returned to sign-in)

request.description: The contract states the sid claim exists specifically so a session can be revoked -- tested here as an immediate rejection, not a delayed one.

exec: pm.test('a revoked session's access token is now rejected', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));
